advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm hardcoding blob/main (vs a version/tag-pinned path) is acceptable given criterion/anchor drift across releases for pinned consumer installs.
evidence: The guide is registry-derived and regenerated in place (registry.py:588 regenerate_criteria_guide); criteria can be added/removed across releases, so `#<criterion-id>` anchors on main may not exist for an older pinned install.
pyproject version is 0.10.0 (pyproject.toml:10) — released/pinned installs are a real audience per the commit's 'consumer install' framing.
advisory.finding: The default docs URL hardcodes the 'main' branch (blob/main/...), so a consumer pinned to an older rebar release gets a coaching deep-link to main's guide, whose criterion set/anchors may have drifted from the installed version.
scenarios: A consumer pinned to nava-rebar 0.9.x whose installed registry has a criterion later renamed/removed on main follows a coaching guide_url and lands on a missing/wrong anchor.

merged_from: The hardcoded default deep-link (blob/main/docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md#<criterion-id>) depends on docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md existing on main with headings that GitHub slugs to lowercase criterion ids; no documentation/check ties the anchor form to the actual guide's headings, risking dead deep-links if the guide's heading format changes.

REBAR_DOCS_URL is an operator-facing override env var, but the change does not add or update any user/operator documentation describing it and the new hosted default; operators cannot discover how to point deep-links at an internal fork/host.
